overview_markdown:
KafClaw is a Go-based agent coordination framework that uses Apache Kafka as its communication backbone. Rather than being a personal assistant like OpenClaw, it is an infrastructure layer for running distributed swarms of autonomous agents, with a structured topic hierarchy (`group.<name>.requests`, `.responses`, `.traces`, `.control.roster`, etc.) and typed message envelopes carrying correlation IDs and timestamps for full observability.

Its core contributions include enterprise-ready agent messaging, hierarchical orchestration, shared memory topics, distributed skill routing, and an agent onboarding protocol — all decoupled from any specific LLM provider or runtime. It is part of a broader Scalytics-backed stack (KafScale, GitClaw, Scalytics Copilot) aimed at private, self-hosted AI operations.

Compared to OpenClaw, KafClaw trades approachability for scale: it has no chat-app channels, skills marketplace, or consumer UI, but offers durable, auditable, distributed coordination that OpenClaw's local-first model doesn't target. The project shows healthy engineering hygiene (CI with fuzzing, CodeQL, active Dependabot merges, a v1.0.0 release) but has a very small community so far.
